automatically checks the document for errors. The errors and warnings reported by the validation engine include problems in the following areas:
The structural integrity and well-formedness of the document.
A set of best-practice rules (such as a maximum number of words in a paragraph).

section.title: Presenting Validation Problems in the Editing Panel
section.p: In the editing panel, validation errors are underlined in red, while warnings are underlined in yellow. On a desktop device, if you hover the mouse pointer over an error or warning, a tooltip is displayed with more information about the problem.

section.title: Validation Side Panel
section.p: Details about validation problems are also shown in the Validation side panel. To open the Validation side panel, select the Validation tab in the vertical stripe on the right side of the screen.

A red marker shows the number of errors found in the document. Each detected problem is listed in its own box in this side panel, and each box has a colored border on the left that indicates the type of problem.
Red - Indicates a validation error.
Yellow - Indicates a validation warning.
Blue - Indicates an informational message. If you click (or tap) a validation item in this side panel, that particular problem is highlighted in the editor. Similarly, if the cursor is located at a location in the document where there is a problem, that particular validation item is highlighted in the Validation side panel. The editor and the side panel are automatically synchronized in real time.

section.title: Quick Fixes to Solve Validation Problems
section.p: also supports Quick Fixes, which help you resolve validation issues that appear in XML documents by offering proposals to solve them automatically with a single click.

For any validation item that has a detected Quick Fix, the proposals are listed as links in the Validation side panel. On a desktop device, these links also appear in the tooltip displayed when you hover over a problem in the editor.
For information about common errors that appear in XML documents that are validated against DTD, XSD, or Relax NG schemas, see Quick Fixes for DTD, XSD, and Relax NG Errors.

also supports Schematron Quick Fixes. A developer can create custom Schematron Quick Fixes to help enforce authoring rules and provide quick solutions for fixing errors. For more information, see the Schematron Quick Fixes (SQF) section in the Oxygen XML Editor User Manual. There is also an interesting blog post on this subject available at: .
section.note: Quick Fixes cannot be applied to read-only documents.
